skeleton:
Builder's Breakfast

British · Easy · Serves 1 (very hungry)

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The plate that built Britain: the mid-morning "builder's" served from vans and caffs to scaffolders, plasterers and roofers since the post-war years. It is a full English with the volume turned up and the fripperies stripped out — double eggs, extra bread fried in the fat, beans and sausage doing the heavy lifting, no garnish, no apology — served with a mug of builder's tea strong enough to stand a spoon in. The plate exists to fuel six hours of physical work, and it does its job without ceremony. The method is the café fry-up's sequence at maximum economy, and the recipe's one refinement is the fat discipline: everything cooks in the one pan, the fried bread drinks what the bacon renders, and the eggs baste in what remains. One pan, one plate, twenty minutes.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

The plate

Fat and seasoning

The tea

  • one builder's mug
- **The tea brews first** — it needs 3–4 minutes steeping while the fry cooks, so it's pouring as the plate lands. Builder's tea is a separate skill: strong, tan-not-brown, with enough milk to make it a drink rather than a test. - **Bread and bacon out of the fridge 15 minutes ahead.** Cold ingredients on a hot pan cook unevenly and this plate has no slack in it. - One plate, warmed — in the oven at its lowest (about 100 °C) or on top of the warm pan, handle off.

Builder's Breakfast

Prep: 5 minutes · Cook: 20 minutes · Total: 25 minutes · Serves 1 (very hungry)

Ingredients

The plate

  • 3 pork sausages (240 g), pricked once each
  • 3 rashers (150 g) back bacon
  • 3 large eggs (165 g)
  • 2 thick slices (100 g) white bread, for fried bread
  • 200 g baked beans (half a tin)
  • 100 g button mushrooms, halved
  • 2 slices (100 g) black pudding (optional but traditional)

Fat and seasoning

  • 10 ml / 10 g neutral oil, to start
  • 10 g butter
  • 3 g fine sea salt
  • 1 g black pepper
  • Brown breakfast sauce, generously applied

The tea

  • 2 tea bags (or 4 g loose leaf), 300 ml just-boiled water, 50 ml milk — one builder's mug

Instructions

  1. **Sausages first, 10 minutes.** Film the pan with oil over medium heat and brown the sausages all over, turning every 3 minutes, dropping the heat if they spit hard. Checkpoint — browned on all sides, juices clear at a nick, the pan holding its first rendered slick.
  2. **Bacon, then black pudding and mushrooms, 6 minutes.** Add the bacon to the pan's fat, press flat for 10 seconds so it doesn't curl, and cook 2–3 minutes a side until the fat renders glassy. Add the black pudding and mushrooms for the last 4 minutes, turning the pudding once. Checkpoint — bacon flat and amber-edged, pudding crusted and intact, mushrooms browned and glossy.
  3. **Fried bread in the fat, 3 minutes.** Lay the bread into the pan's accumulated fat, press flat, and fry 90 seconds a side until deep gold. Checkpoint — both slices golden and crisp-edged, the pan's excess fat now largely drunk by the bread — this is the plate's fuel reserve.
  4. **Eggs basted, 2–3 minutes; beans on the hob alongside.** Clear the pan's centre, add the butter, and crack in the eggs when it foams — basting the hot fat over the whites until set, yolks running. The beans warm in their own small pan with a splash of water and a stir, 4–5 minutes. Checkpoint — whites set with lace fringes, yolks liquid; beans hot and thickened slightly, not skinned.
  5. **The plate.** Beans to one side (contained — they must not reach the eggs), then eggs, bacon, sausages, pudding, mushrooms, and the two fried breads propped at the edge. Pepper over the eggs, brown sauce across the bacon, tea poured. Checkpoint — the finished plate is heft over style — every zone full, the tea steaming beside it, and enough food that the last fried bread is mopping the plate clean.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Plate greasy rather than crispFat poured onto the plate with the foodFried bread drinks the surplus before the eggs go in — sequence, not restraint
Everything ready but the beansBeans left to the endBeans on from step 3; they want 5 minutes at a murmur
Bacon curledNot pressed at contactThe 10-second flat press, immediately
Tea stewed and bitterBoiled, not steepedWater just off the boil, 3–4 minutes, bags out — builder's is strong, not stewed

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- **This plate is eaten the moment it lands** — the whole point. There are no leftovers worth discussing and no make-ahead: the builder's breakfast is a now dish. - **Variation — the scaffolder's double:** 4 eggs, 3 sausages, extra fried bread; the same pan sequence, 4 minutes longer at the egg stage in two shifts. - **Variation — the healthy site hut:** one fried bread dropped, mushrooms doubled, tomato half added — the modern site's nod to longevity. - **The mug:** builder's tea is its own record; the short version is strong tea, properly steeped, properly milky, taken with the plate and refilled before it's empty.
